bug_semantics: The constant-integer for-loop optimizer bound the script loop variable to a native stack-local int through var(&i). ChaiScript's intentional := reference-assignment semantics could copy that reference into ret; after the optimized-loop lambda returned, ret (including a value returned through async/future) still pointed at the destroyed stack slot. Converting fut.get() during string interpolation then dereferenced the dangling numeric pointer in Boxed_Number::get_as<int>(), producing garbage or an ASan-invalid read/segmentation fault.
flaw_origin: Commit 683164650a462b6d5ea58bb899f4c2e668243a1d, 'Add ability to compile for loops', first added the specialized compiled-for-loop path in include/chaiscript/language/chaiscript_parser.hpp and created 'int i = for_loop_params.start; t_ss.add_object(for_loop_params.id, var(&i));'. Later commit ff2ab6bb8dfc72f89128382d73b7d36ebcb4630a merely moved that existing mechanism into chaiscript_optimizer.hpp, so it is not the BIC.

Version boundary: vulnerable lines are absent from v5.8.6, present at v6.0.0 optimizer.hpp:390-391, and `git tag --contains 683164650a462b6d5ea58bb899f4c2e668243a1d --sort=version:refname` yields v6.0.0, v6.1.0, wasm-latest; this supports affected numbered releases 6.0.0 through 6.1.0, consistent with the advisory's 'up to 6.1.0'. Fix PR https://github.com/ChaiScript/ChaiScript/pull/671 has direct member 6dc28ca1baebb0483e608e8caf94d8be7d0cf044, whose optimizer diff replaces the stack local/var(&i) with owning Boxed_Value bv_i(start_int), a reference into its owned storage, and add_object(id,bv_i); later member 276fa9d13a5d0ee3220361625d4e7b3b78cdbf6b reverted only the proposed := semantic change while retaining the optimizer fix. GitHub reports PR #671 squash-merged as 07d62aae9976528a93f5d6ca716c4fe79a808dc5 on 2026-04-12. In the clone, its parent 5a6050210da1cfe579fe00714261067d7e00c496 still has int i/var(&i), while the fix commit has Boxed_Value bv_i/add_object(id,bv_i). `git tag --contains 07d62aae9976528a93f5d6ca716c4fe79a808dc5` is empty, so the fix is on develop but in no available release tag.
reasoning: The reported sink in boxed_number.hpp is where the dangling pointer is observed, not where it is created. History identifies the causal lifetime error ten years earlier: the new compiled loop represented a script-visible loop counter by a non-owning Boxed_Value around a C++ lambda-stack int. The established := alias behavior made that reference escape, and async/future retrieval after the worker/loop frame ended made the stale pointer observable during numeric string conversion. Both -L and exact -S history reject later formatting and the 2016 optimizer-file split as mere transformations and select atomic commit 683164650a462b6d5ea58bb899f4c2e668243a1d; its immediate parent's tree directly lacks the optimizer and vulnerable binding. The landing fix changes the counter to Boxed_Value-owned storage without changing := semantics; the first PR member is the direct code fix and 07d62aae9976528a93f5d6ca716c4fe79a808dc5 is the repository's squash landing commit. The numbered affected-release boundary is v6.0.0-v6.1.0, and no tag contains the fix. Finally, the BIC commit object is a 2016 human-authored/committed commit with no AI marker, so later leftibot/Claude evidence on the 2026 fix is deliberately excluded and the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI.
